newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen strong in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen strong in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to remain strong at auctions in Sydney and Fremantle this week, with about 58,800 bales on offer, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.

Exporters expected auction prices to continue to firm, but are expressing increasing concern at the rate at which prices have increased over recent weeks, the council said in its weekly market preview.
The eastern market indicator has risen by 40 cents a kg clean in the three weeks of selling since Easter, including a 19 cent rise to 659 cents a kg last week.
"The ideal situation would be to have continuous but smaller increments in prices from week to week," the council said.

Continuing strong sales of stockpile wool, with Wool International selling about 28,000 bales last week, including further sales for delivery in the December 1997 quarter, further illustrate the current strength of demand, particularly for finer micron wool, the council said.
